svg.aria-label: Animated comparison of what sets lru_ref, shown as two panels that run in step. A hot page H, created first, and a cold page C each map one 2 MiB region. Creation sets both bits, and the clock hand clears them. H keeps being used, but most accesses are hits KVM never sees; a first touch faults and fills an entry. (a) Marked only on creation, H's bit stays 0, and when the hand returns it zaps the older H. (b) Marked on fill too, the fill sets H's bit again, so the hand keeps H and zaps cold C.

g.text: Each row shows part of a last-level shadow page (512 entries).
H and C look alike: FIFO order
cold C zapped, hot H kept
H and C each map one 2 MiB region. H was created first.
Creating a page sets its lru_ref to 1.
The hand clears H's bit and skips it: a second chance.
Then it does the same for C.
Most of H's accesses are hits, which KVM never sees.
A first touch of a 4 KiB page faults, and KVM fills an entry.
Only (b) marks the page when it fills an entry.
The hand returns to H first, since H is older.
In (b), the hand moves on and zaps cold C instead.
Marking on creation can't tell hot from cold; marking on fill can.
